clue.text: Quite good at rectifying odd trim in defect

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for a defect

parts.note: a failing is a defect or weakness

indicators.note: rectifying means putting right, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone praises a tailor for fixing a strange trim in a faulty garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite good at' looks like the definition, but 'at' is only a link. 'rectifying' makes RTOMIDD from ODD TRIM; 'in' sits it inside the defect.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something passable or moderately good, neither excellent nor poor.

clue.text: Supporter bled crassly when wounded at fun party

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a team or star

indicators.note: wounded suggests damage, so the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A football fan bleeds clumsily after being hurt at a jolly gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crassly' looks like an anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'when wounded' is what rearranges BLED CRASSLY, giving CYDRESSBALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume party where guests dress up is a classic kind of fun party.

clue.text: Nightmare at home with youngster going to America

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a cub is a young animal, or a young Scout
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A bad dream about a child being sent to the States.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an evil spirit thought to weigh on sleepers, hence an oppressive nightmare.

clue.text: Giver of first-hand information may take a bit

definitions.meaning: getting news straight from the source, the original informant
the part of a riding animal that holds the metal bit of a bridle

explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something straight from the source is the idiom, and a bridle's bit sits in the animal's jaws.

clue.text: Change one first into analgesic

parts.note: to morph is to change shape or form
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: Turn something into a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphia is an old name for morphine, a powerful painkiller.

clue.text: Basic position is "can't pay, won't pay"

definitions.meaning: the setting a system adopts unless told otherwise
failing to meet a debt or repayment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the standard preset option and a failure to repay what is owed.

clue.text: Yarn from Cornwall is legendary

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tale from the West Country of England, a land famous for myths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' tempts as a story; here it is a fine thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread used for stockings, a type of yarn.

clue.text: Unpleasant number one with a few more

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
some means a few, as in 'have some more'

explanation.surface: The favourite song, alongside several more hits, is hard to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells, so thoroughly disagreeable.

clue.text: One little climber on board with head with character that can't be copied

indicators.note: in a down clue a climber goes upwards, so the preceding pieces read from the bottom up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
mini means little
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A small mountaineer on a ship's deck, leading the way, shows unique character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' turns IMINI upwards to give INIMI, which sits on TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being impossible to imitate is exactly a character beyond copying.

clue.text: Source of fuel in cars is on

definitions.text: Source of fuel in cars is on

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are the raw source from which the answer is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something powers a car once it is switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FUEL IN CARS IS ON rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue describes splitting atoms to release energy, though strictly it is power rather than fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting heavy atoms releases the energy used in power stations, a source of power.

clue.text: See 9
Bad boy may develop into booby

indicators.note: develop suggests changing form, so the letters of booby are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish child may grow up into a delinquent.
explanation.definitionFit: A yobbo is British slang for a loutish, badly behaved young man.

clue.text: Where to receive ideas etc for 45 minutes on return of old almanac

parts.note: three quarters of an hour, so three of the four letters of the word hour

indicators.note: return means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Old Moore's Almanack is a long-running British book of predictions

explanation.surface: A place to keep ideas, given three quarters of an hour after an old yearbook comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return of' reads MOORES backwards as SEROOM. Old Moore's Almanack is an annual British book of astrological forecasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something houseroom is to accept or entertain it, as in 'I wouldn't give that idea houseroom'.

clue.text: Able to withstand boy going into exam again

indicators.note: going into shows one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a resit is a second attempt at an exam
Stan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad sits a test a second time and holds up under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistant describes something that holds out against an attack or force.

clue.text: Corn with temperature

parts.note: heat is temperature, as in 'turn up the heat'

explanation.surface: Grain is grown in a hot climate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage corn is a general word for cereal crops, especially wheat.

clue.text: It doesn't say how rich Strafford was when he departed

parts.note: went is the past of go, departed
worth is a person's wealth, how rich they are

explanation.surface: A remark that history does not record the Earl's fortune at his death.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Wentworth, 1st Earl of Strafford, was a minister of Charles I executed in 1641.
explanation.definitionFit: Strafford's family name was Wentworth; he was created Earl of Strafford in 1640.

clue.text: Island of the south with prophet

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A southern island associated with a biblical prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean, birthplace of Pythagoras.

clue.text: Letter to girl No 4 and No 5?

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
IV is the Roman numeral for four
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A note sent to a young lady, numbered four and five.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a letter or written message, usually a long or official one.

clue.text: Fluffed lines in female part aimed at casting off her shackles

definitions.text: aimed at casting off her shackles

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the female part

parts.note: the womb is a part of a woman's body

indicators.note: an actor who fluffs lines gets them wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An actress muffs her script while playing a feminist role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluffed' makes ENSLI, and 'in' puts it within the female part. The definition is an adjectival description of the movement's aim rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's liberation movement campaigned for women to be freed from social restrictions.

clue.text: See what's in the box?

definitions.meaning: a person giving evidence stands in the courtroom box

explanation.definitionFit: To witness is to see, and a witness gives evidence from the witness box in court.

clue.text: Formulating centre piece to one of mixed race

indicators.note: the central portion of the word is taken, losing letters at both ends

explanation.surface: Devising the core of something for a person of mixed heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre piece' takes MULAT from the middle of FORMULATING; TO is taken as written. The word is now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the term described a person with one Black and one white parent, a dated and offensive word.

clue.text: Some Irish fliers with others connected with the tongue

indicators.note: only some of the airline's name is used, with letters dropped from each end

parts.note: Aer Lingus is the Irish national airline
al, as in et al, means and others

explanation.surface: Some Irish air travellers join others in talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' strips AER and S from AERLINGUS, leaving LINGU.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingual means relating to the tongue or to speech.

clue.text: Meets trouble: god is about, going to lead, say

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the god's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Baal is a Canaanite god

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone runs into problems when a deity intervenes, bound for the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as a verb but is the metal; 'say' marks it as an example. 'trouble' makes SEMET, and 'is about' has the god surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a common, non-precious metal.

clue.text: See 3
Success for church to exhibit pain

parts.note: a win is a success
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A triumph for the church brings visible suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to flinch or grimace, outwardly showing pain.

clue.text: Free time that is cluttered with rules

indicators.note: cluttered suggests disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Spare hours become messy when full of regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is time spent away from work, spare hours to use as you please.

clue.text: Rotter universally condemned for using this?

definitions.text: Rotter universally condemned for using this?

indicators.note: condemned suggests something ruined, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A villain is reviled by everyone for inflicting cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' rearranges ROTTER plus U, and the whole clue describes the crime that would earn universal condemnation.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflicting severe pain is the cruelty for which a scoundrel would be condemned.

clue.text: Parliamentarian with his leading man less than less of a fiend

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
taken as written
top means leading, as in top dog
he is a male person

indicators.note: less than means shortened, so the word loses a letter

explanation.surface: An MEP's lead actor is something below even a lesser demon.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the devil to whom Faust sold his soul, the archetypal fiend.
